target_customer: pharmaceutical partners and acquirers; ultimately patients with depression and other mental-health disorders
problem: Existing treatments for depression and other psychiatric disorders work poorly for many patients; the company designs new chemical entities based on psychedelic chemistry to improve efficacy and duration.
business_model: drug development funded by venture capital, with value realised through licensing and sale of programs to pharma
product_category: clinical-stage biotech: psychedelic-derived therapeutics for mental health

founders.name: Jonathan Sporn
founders.background_notes: Former chief of psychiatry in the Boston area per YC page.

founders.name: Andrew Kruegel
founders.background_notes: Medicinal chemist and pharmacologist with IP and fundraising experience, per YC page.

founders.name: Dalibor Sames
founders.background_notes: Synthetic and medicinal chemist; iboga and mitragynine chemistry.

competitors.name: Compass Pathways
competitors.traction_then: listed on Nasdaq in 2020 per a secondary source

competitors.name: MindMed
competitors.what: psychedelic and related drug development for mental health

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing novel chemical entities and taking them through clinical trials is research-grade; the company reported Phase 2 data for its lead drug (10 mg dose cut MADRS by 21.6 points versus 12.1 for low dose).

defensibility.rationale: New chemical entities with an explicit IP strategy and clinical data are hard to copy, though other psychedelic biotechs pursue the same indications.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: AbbVie signed a licensing partnership with Gilgamesh in May 2024 and in August 2025 agreed to acquire the bretisilocin program for up to $1.2B, with remaining assets spun into a new entity.

market_need_then: Depression treatment gaps and a 2020 investor wave into psychedelic medicine (Compass and MindMed listings) created demand for differentiated compounds.
outcome_analysis: Gilgamesh combined an experienced psychiatry and medicinal-chemistry founding team with new chemical entities, raised a $39M Series B led by Prime Movers Lab in December 2022, and produced Phase 2 data for bretisilocin. AbbVie then partnered in 2024 and agreed in August 2025 to buy the program for up to $1.2B, an outcome driven by technical results and IP rather than a company-wide exit; the remaining team continues in a spin-out.
notes: Only the Series B was found as a priced round; earlier rounds exist (Prime Movers Lab 'invested again'; one report puts total near $74M at Series B, CB Insights lists $83.45M over 9 rounds) but were not itemised. AbbVie deal is a program sale, not a company acquisition: the YC status remains Active, so exit is recorded as none; upfront amount was undisclosed.
